records.text: Spencer Cox said investigators were shown Discord messages between Tyler Robinson and his roommate about retrieving and hiding a rifle, engraved bullets, a scope, and changing outfits.
records.speaker: Spencer Cox

appearances.snippet: Investigators identified an individual as the roommate of Robinson. Investigators interviewed that roommate, who stated that his roommate, referring to Robinson, made a joke on Discord. ... Investigators asked if he would show them the messages on Discord. He opened it and showed several messages to investigators and allowed investigators to take photos of the screen as each message was shown by Robinson's roommate. ... These photos consisted of various messages, including content of messages between the phone contact name Tyler with an emoji icon and Robinson's roommate's device. The content of these messages included messages affiliated with the contact Tyler stating a need to retrieve a rifle from a drop point, leaving the rifle in a bush. ... Messages related to a to visually watching the area where a rifle was left and a message referring to having left the rifle wrapped in a towel. ... The messages also refer to engraving bullets and a mention of a scope and the rifle being unique. ... Messages from the contact Tyler also mentioned that he had changed outfits.

verification.notes: The statement accurately summarizes the public press briefing: Cox described the roommate showing investigators purported Discord messages concerning a rifle drop point, a bush and towel, engravings, a scope, and changed clothing. Later reporting clarified that some described communications did not appear to be Discord messages, but the statement is about what Cox said.

records.text: Breland reported that the clipping company paid subcontractors, many from poorer countries in Eastern Europe and the global south, to turn supplied videos into short clips, and that clipping services often used Discord to attract clippers while concealing feed manipulation.
records.speaker: Ali Breland

appearances.snippet: We continue with the article. The company pays subcontractors, many from poorer countries in Eastern Europe and the global south, to chop up videos that the company provides into bite-sized pieces in the hopes that the clips will go viral online. ... Many video clipping services operate in relative secrecy so that the public is not aware of the manipulation of their social media feeds. ... But the services also need to attract potential clippers. They typically rely on chat servers, on Discord, an internet messaging app that was initially developed for gamers.

records.text: Breland reported joining Elephant Clipping’s Discord after an anonymous tip and seeing payments for videos posted from accounts designed to resemble ordinary Americans spontaneously supporting the GOP; he described the operation as astroturfing.
records.speaker: Ali Breland

appearances.snippet: After Anonymous Tipster flagged elephant clipping to me, I was able to access its Discord server and other related political clipping campaign chats just by clicking join, noting on a forum that I was based in the U.S., and answering some questions about my availability and desire to clip. ... Once I was in, I could see the mechanics of the campaign, which pays huge sums of money to people, many of whom appeared to be outside of the U.S. ... to push video clips from accounts that are designed to look like those of ordinary Americans spontaneously touting reasons to favor the GOP. ... Elephant Clippings operation is the newest version of astroturfing. Orchestrated messaging designed to look like genuine expressions of grassroots support, many of these campaigns involve private chat rooms, and Matt Serviuos seems to have been running the campaign for some time.

links.title: What led here and what followed

records.notes: Deace characterized the record as containing three confessions: to Robinsons parents, to his roommate, and on Discord.

records.text: Cox described Discord messages
records.speaker: Spencer Cox

appearances.snippet: Investigators identified an individual as the roommate of Robinson. Investigators interviewed that roommate, who stated that his roommate, referring to Robinson, made a joke on Discord. ... Investigators asked if he would show them the messages on Discord. He opened it and showed several messages to investigators and allowed investigators to take photos of the screen as each message was shown by Robinson's roommate. ... These photos consisted of various messages, including content of messages between the phone contact name Tyler with an emoji icon and Robinson's roommate's device. The content of these messages included messages affiliated with the contact Tyler stating a need to retrieve a rifle from a drop point, leaving the rifle in a bush. ... Messages related to a to visually watching the area where a rifle was left and a message referring to having left the rifle wrapped in a towel. ... The messages also refer to engraving bullets and a mention of a scope and the rifle being unique. ... Messages from the contact Tyler also mentioned that he had changed outfits.

links.title: What led here and what followed

records.notes: Cox said investigators viewed Discord messages about a rifle, ammunition, scope, and clothing.

He's reading from a piece of paper and then the feds got caught lying and then they altered things and they said, we always said that it was eye messages.

records.notes: Owens accused authorities of changing the message platform from Discord to iMessage after Discord's public statement.

records.text: Wilson campaign shift
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: I debated Andrew Wilson on August 14th, to be specific. So this campaign had its instructions changed. They wanted people to stop clipping generic Charlie Kirk and to instead focus on clipping Andrew Wilson to make him look good. ... I kid you not. Again, they communicated these instructions over Discord. So here is what was communicated from elephant clipping. ... about the sudden campaign shift, which was going to last one week. So they were offering $75,000. That's the pool. ... for people to try to make Andrew Wilson look good. No easy feat, you can see. And then they're getting frustrated because people are not acknowledging this campaign change, this campaign change.

links.title: What led here and what followed

records.notes: Owens says the campaign changed after her August 14 debate to a one-week push making Andrew Wilson look good, with a $75,000 pool communicated on Discord.

records.text: Reporter describes astroturf
records.speaker: Ali Breland

appearances.snippet: After Anonymous Tipster flagged elephant clipping to me, I was able to access its Discord server and other related political clipping campaign chats just by clicking join, noting on a forum that I was based in the U.S., and answering some questions about my availability and desire to clip. ... Once I was in, I could see the mechanics of the campaign, which pays huge sums of money to people, many of whom appeared to be outside of the U.S. ... to push video clips from accounts that are designed to look like those of ordinary Americans spontaneously touting reasons to favor the GOP. ... Elephant Clippings operation is the newest version of astroturfing. Orchestrated messaging designed to look like genuine expressions of grassroots support, many of these campaigns involve private chat rooms, and Matt Serviuos seems to have been running the campaign for some time.

links.title: What led here and what followed

records.notes: Breland, in the article read by Owens, says he entered Elephant Clipping’s Discord and observed paid clips posted from accounts designed to resemble ordinary Americans spontaneously supporting the GOP.

records.text: Campaign removals reported
records.speaker: Ali Breland

appearances.snippet: Steve Wynn, Blake (Blake Wynn)'s uncle, did not respond to a request for comment. Shortly after I first reached out to both Wynn's, Enclave and Key and others that were involved in the campaigns, the deletions started. ... By Thursday afternoon, video folders for clippers that had been uploaded to a Google Drive by Katz (Jules Katz) and O'Hara (Jack O'Hara) had disappeared. ... Though the same files were then posted by Goodman (Benjamin Goodman), who used an email address not linked to Enclave and Key, the Discord channels for U.S. politics clipping and elephant clipping were also delisted from the publicly visible campaigns in the ClipSon and Clip It discords. The Campaigns were still visible on Monster Lab, but descriptions explaining the purpose of each campaign were gone. ... On Friday morning, Enclave and Key's Google Drives for the campaigns were taken down as well. Blake Wynn has connections beyond his uncle in the conservative media sphere.

links.title: What led here and what followed

records.notes: Breland reports that after inquiries, uploader-linked folders disappeared or were reposted with another email, campaign listings and descriptions were removed, and Enclave and Key campaign Drives were taken down.
